data.body:
## Follow-up landed: AC2 and AC7 closed properly

The completion verifier refused the first close, and it was right to. Two acceptance
criteria were not actually met by change 1429, and both failures were of the same kind --
work that LOOKED done because its correct output was invisible.

**AC2 (RED-first proof).** The RED half was only ever demonstrated transiently while
working; nothing in the tree recorded it. So the repo could not show the bug had been
real, and no test would have caught a regression of the resolver back to bare-name
matching -- the very defect under repair.

`tests/scripts/pre_fix_config_read_gate.py` now freezes the pre-fix gate (the global
`set[str]` of attribute names and the `field_name in reads` test), copied from the commit
before the fix. It is fixture-only; nothing under `src/` imports it, and its value is that
it still contains the bug. `tests/scripts/test_check_config_reads_red_proof.py` runs that
snapshot and the live gate against the SAME synthetic schema and asserts they disagree:
the old gate silently passes an inert `CodeHealthConfig.enabled` whose bare name is read on
`UiConfig`; the live gate fires on it. A control case pins the asymmetry the report
described -- a uniquely-named inert field fires on BOTH versions, which is why `analyzers`
needed a marker while its neighbour slipped through -- so the differential is attributable
to owner resolution and not to some unrelated change.

**AC7 (markers pointing at tickets).** No such logic was ever written. `check` only
validated that a pointer was non-empty. This was easy to miss precisely because the
correct output on today's tree is EMPTY: a reporter that has never emitted anything is
indistinguishable from one that does not exist. My earlier report claimed this criterion
was satisfied by having manually observed the empty result -- that was a hand-check of the
schema, not an implementation, and it should not have been presented as the latter.

`ticket_pointer_reports()` now surfaces them and `main()` prints them without touching the
exit code: whether a parked marker is still justified depends on its ticket's state, which
a CI gate cannot know, so it reports rather than fails. The rationale for having it at all
is that such a marker EXPIRES when its ticket closes -- `analyzers` carried `# read-via:
inert pending bug dce2-...`, and dce2 has since closed -- so without the report these
become permanent by default. Tests cover the full and short id forms, the print path, the
advisory exit code, and the real schema's currently-empty result.

**Mutation-checked.** Each new artifact was verified to have teeth: regressing the resolver
to bare-name matching, neutering the reporter, and "fixing" the frozen snapshot each
return the relevant tests to RED.

Gerrit change 1431: LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, zero unresolved, merged. On merged main the
gate passes and `tests/scripts` is green at 604 passed / 1 skipped, including all eight new
tests.

Nothing about the reported findings changed: the four newly-flagged fields and their
factual markers stand as reported, and no field was triaged.
